correctness.rationale: Source Algorithm 1 reduces on nonzero singleton sketches to exact line searches along the fixed one-predecessor H-orthogonalized coordinate basis. The rank-drop lemma proves the full-sweep product vanishes exactly for a mutually H-conjugate basis; recursive support proves equivalence with tridiagonal H. Genericity follows by an adjoint projection argument. In three dimensions direct Gram products produce D, W and the exact factor |c|/sqrt(aW), with strict inequality from SPD and exact rational witness. Symbolic, exact-rational and reproducible random calculations were rerun from the included script. The theorem does not assert anything for zero-gradient exceptional branches or arbitrary IID sketch sequences.

value.rationale: The locality of the conjugacy correction is central to the sparse RCGLS method. The theorem gives a complete graph-theoretic classification of when a single pass of d column touches is exact, and the first quantitative obstruction when the sparsity order violates that condition: a long-range coupling controls the entire third-step remaining energy, and a permutation switches a near-stagnating sweep into an exact one. This motivates sparse-column ordering and differentiates local from global conjugacy in actual iterative linear solvers. It is not presented as a generic textbook conjugate-directions lemma or an arbitrary sliced invariant.
